$comment: Advisories deliberately NOT fixed, each with a reason and a review date.
Read by scripts/audit-gate.mjs: anything in the tree that is NOT listed
here fails the Security Scan, and any entry past its reviewBy also fails.
An acceptance that never expires is a permanent blind spot.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS instead of a plain `npm audit --audit-level=high`:
every real project accumulates advisories it cannot fix today (dev-only
tooling needing a semver-major bump, a transitive pin three levels down).
A raw audit fails on those forever, and a permanently-red blocking gate is
worse than no gate -- a genuine finding becomes indistinguishable from the
standing noise. Carving accepted ids out explicitly restores the property
that matters: a NEW vulnerability fails the run.
Adding an entry is a security DECISION, not a way to quiet the build.
Justify why the vulnerable code path is unreachable in this product.
NEVER blanket `npm audit fix` (forced or not) to clear a finding -- it
resolves transitive deps outside their declared ranges and can introduce
more advisories than it removes. Diff the lockfile after any audit fix and
revert if the changed-package set is not what you expected to touch.
An empty list is the goal state, not a missing file.
Entry shape:
{ "id": "GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx", "package": "name",
"reason": "why this path is unreachable here",
"reviewBy": "YYYY-MM-DD" }
